kind.issue: identical to layer at the first node
kind.wait: each node: psx_cache_attendi_kinds(bit of the kind it consumes) before the post-wait barrier; reads of later kinds stay in flight (reserved: ready == false, pinned) while earlier nodes compute

layer.issue: first expert node of the layer event: psx_cache_avvia for every (kind, expert), kinds ordered [node kind, then gate, up, down], experts ascending, claimed dynamically from one shared counter
layer.pins: released by each thread at the start of every expert node; later nodes re-acquire the slices as hits (psx_cache_avvia -> HIT)
layer.wait: every thread psx_cache_attendi (all its reads) before the post-wait barrier, at every node

layer_touch.issue: identical to layer at the first node (same claim order, same counter)
layer_touch.pins: held for the whole layer event; released at the next event's first node after waiting for any read still pending; later nodes psx_cache_touch each slice in the baseline claim order (same LRU move as a hit, no pin, no wait)
layer_touch.wait: every thread psx_cache_attendi_kinds(all kinds) at the first node (baseline placement)

causal_information: only the router decision of the current layer, already consumed by the baseline hook; no prediction, no lookahead across layers, no new thread, no tunable parameter
fail_closed: explicit ARGINE_EXPERT_WAIT with ARGINE_PREFETCH set to anything but 0

implementation_choices.barrier_placement: unchanged: one barrier before issue (after the shared counter reset by thread 0), one after the wait; no barrier added or removed
implementation_choices.event_identity: per-thread psx_semantic_event_tracker (same layer and kind not yet seen = same event); deterministic and identical on every thread because every thread runs every node
implementation_choices.failure_handling: a failed read is fatal at the node that waits for it (GGML_ABORT), as in the baseline; an invalid or unrealisable arm aborts at startup
implementation_choices.handle_release_point: the thread's borrowed file handle is released, and its pending-read deque cleared, only when none of its reads is pending; entries are marked finished, never erased from the middle (the kernel holds OVERLAPPED addresses)
implementation_choices.kind_unknown_at_first_node: a kind whose tensor position is not yet registered at the first node is issued at its own node and waited there, as the baseline does
implementation_choices.pin_release_point: C0 and C: at the next layer event's first expert node, after waiting for any read of the thread still pending (counted as orphan_pending, must be 0)
implementation_choices.touch_order: C0 and C later nodes: psx_cache_touch over the same (kind, expert) claim sequence the baseline re-acquires, distributed by the same shared counter
implementation_choices.trace_layout: one T record per thread per expert node in every arm (INSTRUMENTATION_SCHEMA.json); I records unchanged in format; config keys expert_wait, expert_wait_explicit, ets_schema
implementation_choices.wait_primitive: per read GetOverlappedResult(bWait=TRUE) on the thread's borrowed handle, as psx_cache_attendi; with tracing, WaitForMultipleObjects one completion at a time first (as the baseline's arx_wait_precise)

invariants: same slices requested, same claim order, same bytes read
same LRU access sequence (touch == hit recency move); hit COUNTERS differ by construction
same pinned footprint: the layer's slices, as in the baseline; in-flight slots are reserved (ready == false) and never evictable
budget unchanged; budget violations must stay 0
layout_decision: R1-R4 runtime sources in patches/ are hash-locked by the consolidation manifest; R5 sources are an additive copy in patches/r5-ets/ and the binary identity is llama-research-r5-ets/BUILD-INFO.json
read_compute_overlap: kind only: between the first expert node's wait and the waits of the second and third expert nodes of the same layer, reads of the later kinds are in flight (OVERLAPPED I/O needs no CPU thread) while ggml computes the earlier nodes
selector: ARGINE_EXPERT_WAIT = layer | layer_touch | kind (unset = layer); anything else aborts
